text:
tara: thinking out loud — proposing a lightweight "precision scheduler" shim in the runtime that picks FP8/INT8/4bit variants per-batch based on latency SLOs + recent quality drift. goal: centralized cheap heuristics, not a heavyweight rl controller.

ajay: sounds useful. how is this different from the router policies we already have?

tara: good q. router picks model variant by route/region/tier. this shim lives inside the serving node and makes per-batch micro-decisions when multiple compatible variants are available (same arch + quantized weights). it considers queue depth, tail latency, and "quality budget" for the request key.

kevin: "quality budget"? define plz.

tara: basically a short-lived token that tracks allowed degradation for a traffic slice. example: background embedding jobs get high budget for 4-bit, interactive chat has tiny budget. it's computed from route config + recent evals.

sasha: i like the pragmatic approach. my worry: reproducibility and cache/KV behavior when switching precision mid-session.

tara: yep. plan: disallow precision changes for sessions with KV cache active (chat streaming). shim only does per-batch precision for stateless generation or for new sessions. if we need session-level rollback, we pin precision for the convo.

ajay: what's the API footprint? we shouldn't force all callers to pass budgets.

tara: shim uses route metadata + workload tags. optional header: X-Precision-Budget can override for advanced clients. default fallback is route-level config in console.

kevin: can we see a config sketch?

tara: paste:

```yaml
precision_scheduler:
  enabled: true
  default_budget: low
  routes:
    /v1/chat: {budget: tiny, allowed: [fp16, int8]}
    /v1/embeddings: {budget: high, allowed: [int4, int8, fp8]}
  heuristics:
    - name: latency_slo
      threshold_ms: 120
    - name: recent_eval_penalty
      window_minutes: 60
```

kevin: ok. what about telemetry? need signals to avoid silent regressions.

tara: telemetry: per-precision token-level quality deltas (via our eval harness hooks), token latency histograms, and a "precision-fallback" counter with reason codes. surface on per-route dashboard.

sasha: testing plan? we can't ship this without good regression gates.

tara: propose staged rollout: offline sim with replayed traffic + canary with small % of traffic, then progressive ramp. include A/B with our prompt-based evals and automatic rollback if metric crosses guardrails.

ajay: fallback behavior on OOMs and quantization incompatibility?

tara: fallback priority: same-arch higher-precision variant -> different-arch compatible variant -> queue to dedicated pool. must always be able to fail open to a safe (fp16) path.

kevin: operational complexity concern: more knobs for SREs. can we default to conservative heuristics?

tara: yes defaults conservative. ops can flip to aggressive profiles per-customer. also expose a single toggle in Console to disable shim per pool.

runbot: ci/canary check for precision_scheduler branch passed — coverage: unit + integration harness, 42 tests green. :white_check_mark:

ajay: next steps? RFC writeup + proto for config + small POC in runtime-emulator.

tara: i'll draft an RFC today and add perf sims. volunteers for review: @ajay @kevin @sasha. thanks! :rocket:
